run.summary: The replay follows a governed onboarding run from intake gate through final checklist package. The system correctly preserves prerequisite failure, regulated-path classification, legal escalation, security ambiguity, and final stakeholder guidance.

steps.title: R-01 Intake gate
steps.trigger: A vendor onboarding request arrives before the required questionnaire submission is present in the intake package.
steps.summary: The run starts in a blocked posture, waits for human intervention, and resumes only after the required questionnaire is submitted.
questions: Should any downstream domain review be allowed to continue?

subqueries.label: Check required-intake manifest
subqueries.reason: Prerequisite presence is a deterministic gate; it should not be inferred from semantic retrieval.

subqueries.label: Confirm questionnaire status
subqueries.reason: The system checks for a concrete submission event, not a paraphrase.

evidence.note: Defines questionnaire submission as a hard prerequisite for vendor review.
Shows that the request arrived without the questionnaire and was later updated after procurement follow-up.

steps.rationale: The correct behavior is to halt, emit BLOCKED, and wait. The system should not improvise around a missing source.

determination.downstream: Resume classification once the questionnaire is submitted and the run state flips back to active.
output: Human action logged: procurement requested submission
R-01 marked RESOLVED after submission landed

audit: Initial run emitted BLOCKED and halted downstream execution
Human intervention recorded outside the agent loop
Pipeline state reopened after submission timestamp was verified

steps.title: R-02 Path classification
steps.trigger: The questionnaire is now available, so the supervisor can classify the onboarding path and decide whether fast-track remains possible.
steps.summary: The run classifies as REGULATED because the questionnaire indicates EU employee scheduling data and ERP-adjacent data movement.
questions: Does the vendor touch regulated or sensitive data?
Does ERP adjacency alter review posture?

subqueries.label: Determine data class exposure
subqueries.reason: Data-class facts live in the questionnaire, but their implications live in the legal matrix.

subqueries.label: Check integration posture
subqueries.reason: ERP adjacency changes the downstream review shape even when the exact tier is unresolved.

evidence.note: Shows EU employee scheduling data and SAP S/4HANA-related exports in scope.
Maps EU personal data exposure to DPA requirement.
Provides the ERP integration review posture referenced by security.

bundle: Security policy section for integration posture
steps.rationale: The regulated classification is structural. It does not require model creativity once the evidence bundle is assembled correctly.

determination.downstream: Launch domain reviews with fast-track disabled and regulated-path semantics attached to the bundle.
output: ERP adjacency raises downstream review posture

audit: Questionnaire facts read via direct structured access rather than embedding lane
Regulated-path status attached to downstream state object
Fast-track disabled before domain agents ran

steps.title: R-03 Legal review
steps.trigger: The regulated path requires legal review of DPA obligations and NDA execution status before information exchange can proceed.
steps.summary: Legal determines that a GDPR Art. 28 DPA is required and that NDA execution remains unresolved, so human-owned legal work is still open.
questions: Does the evidence fire a DPA requirement?
Is NDA execution confirmed strongly enough to allow information exchange?

subqueries.label: Retrieve DPA trigger rows
subqueries.reason: Legal obligations hinge on exact rows and carveouts, not fuzzy semantic similarity.

subqueries.label: Check NDA execution requirement
subqueries.reason: The system needs the formal clause first and precedent only as supporting context.

evidence.note: These rows make DPA execution mandatory before data exchange for this data class.
States that NDA execution must be confirmed before sensitive information exchange.
Supports the interpretation but does not outrank the policy clause.

steps.rationale: This is not a model failure. The system is doing the correct enterprise thing by surfacing unresolved legal ownership rather than manufacturing closure.

determination.downstream: Checklist must preserve both the DPA blocker and the unresolved NDA requirement.
output: BLOCKER: execute GDPR Art. 28 DPA before data exchange
BLOCKER: NDA execution not yet confirmed
Status remains escalated because resolution is human-owned

audit: Tier 1 legal sources outranked questionnaire claims and precedent notes
No attempt made to convert unresolved legal work into a complete status
Escalation payload forwarded unchanged to checklist assembly

steps.title: R-03 IT Security review
steps.trigger: Security receives the regulated-path bundle and must determine integration posture and any additional follow-up required before implementation can begin.
steps.summary: Security cannot cleanly assign the integration tier from questionnaire evidence alone, so the run preserves the ambiguity and requests architecture artifacts.
questions: Does the questionnaire satisfy a named ERP integration tier?
What follow-up evidence is required to resolve the ambiguity?

subqueries.label: Retrieve integration tier table
subqueries.reason: Tier definitions live in a specific policy section and must be matched exactly.

subqueries.label: Compare vendor integration description
subqueries.reason: The vendor's wording is needed, but it should not outrank the policy table.

evidence.note: Defines the conditions for mediated, indirect, and higher-risk integration tiers.
Describes exports and middleware but leaves the actual technical path ambiguous.
Shows a prior case where questionnaire evidence looked sufficient but required architecture review to resolve.

steps.rationale: This is the demo's key ambiguity case. The right answer is not to guess. It is to preserve uncertainty and route the missing evidence request to a human owner.

determination.downstream: Checklist must request architecture diagram and data-flow documentation within the stated follow-up window.
output: BLOCKER: integration tier remains unclassified pending review
Request architecture diagram and data-flow documents
Fast-track remains false while ambiguity is unresolved

audit: Questionnaire facts were treated as claims, not authoritative classification
Policy tier table remained the governing source
Security ambiguity propagated instead of being softened into a maybe-complete result

steps.title: R-04 Procurement review
steps.trigger: Procurement evaluates approval routing and whether the regulated path forces an executive or exceptional commercial workflow.
steps.summary: Procurement resolves the approval path as standard and confirms that executive approval is not required, while still respecting the escalated items from legal and security.
questions: Which approval path fires for this vendor posture?
Does the regulated path force executive approval?

subqueries.label: Retrieve approval matrix row
subqueries.reason: Approval path should be decided by the matrix row, not inferred from narrative descriptions.

evidence.note: Maps this posture to the standard approval path without executive sign-off.

bundle: Current escalations from legal and security
steps.rationale: A complete procurement answer can coexist with escalations elsewhere. The pipeline needs that nuance rather than flattening everything into one status.

determination.downstream: Pass the resolved approval path into checklist assembly while preserving all upstream blockers.
output: Procurement result complete but overall pipeline still open

audit: Matrix row targeted directly rather than retrieved from a flat index
Procurement completion did not overwrite legal or security escalations
Approval-path result attached to the checklist package

steps.title: R-05/R-06 Checklist and stakeholder guidance
steps.trigger: All domain outputs are available, so the system assembles the final package and determines whether the run can close.
steps.summary: The final package keeps all three blockers visible, cites their sources, and routes next-step guidance to the correct owners. The run ends escalated by design.
questions: Which items are resolved and safe to present as complete?

subqueries.label: Collect upstream determinations
subqueries.reason: Checklist assembly should consume already-governed outputs rather than re-reason over raw documents.

evidence.note: Carries DPA and NDA blockers forward unchanged.
Carries integration-tier ambiguity and architecture-document request forward unchanged.
Provides the standard approval path and no-executive-signoff resolution.

steps.rationale: This is where null-passthrough matters most. A polished final answer that erases upstream ambiguity would be worse than an escalation.

determination.downstream: Deliver blocker list and next-step guidance to Legal, IT Security, Procurement, and the business owner.
output: BLOCKER: confirm NDA execution before information exchange
BLOCKER: classify ERP integration tier after architecture review

audit: Escalated upstream states preserved with null-passthrough discipline
Checklist package split resolved items from blocking items explicitly
Final outcome emitted as ESCALATED rather than forcing a synthetic COMPLETE
